open_points.subject: record_change path policy for SQLite-managed files
open_points.text: - record_change: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links, by os.O_NOFOLLOW on each open; the host is Linux (A18), so no code checks that the flag exists; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
open_points.other_text: - record_change: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] Every row MUST be read and written only through the StoreRepository operations of one SqliteStoreRepository that the module builds over its own connection inside the transaction it began; the module sends no SQL of its own beyond beginning, committing and rolling back that transaction and setting the connection's synchronous mode, and never creates a table itself.
open_points.question: Must the os.O_NOFOLLOW requirement exclude files opened internally by SQLite, such as the database and transaction-journal files, or must the SQLite boundary change to provide an opening mechanism that applies os.O_NOFOLLOW to every such open?
